key_insight: A nonstandard FEM–BEM transmission formulation can solve the London equation in unbounded 3D space and reveal vortex-favorable paths in superconductors.
engineering_relevance: The method enables accurate magnetic-field computation without artificial domain truncation, supporting superconducting design and vortex-nucleation analysis in complex geometries.
method: Reformulate the magnetic potential as a bounded–unbounded transmission problem.
Couple finite elements with boundary elements to compute the exterior magnetic field $H_0$.
Use the Kikuchi mixed formulation and $H(\operatorname{curl})$-conforming FEM to recover the divergence-free field $B_0$.
evidence_signal: The discretization is validated with convergence tests and then applied to the isoflux problem, showing the ball’s diameter is the maximizer while elongated ellipsoids exhibit off-axis competitors with higher isoflux ratios.
watch_item: For highly elongated geometries, rotational symmetry can create non-unique maximizers and a degenerate direction, so interpretation of the isoflux optimum may require care.
paper_title: Numerical approach to the London Equation of superconductivity
